newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 16.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
YADAV WINS TRUST VOTE WITHOUT HITCH

Laloo Prasad Yadav's government in Bihar state won a trust vote amid unruly scenes, securing 168 votes to nil in the 324-member strong state assembly. The Congress party abstained from voting. The opposition parties including the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Janata Dal party boycotted the voting. This is the second time Yadav won a vote of confidence in the state assembly.
The Economic Times
RESERVE BANK INTERVENES TO STEM RUPEE RISE

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened in the foreign exchange markets to stem a rise in the value of the rupee. The move followed the sale of dollars at 35.70 rupees a dollar by the State Bank of India. Expectations of an RBI intervention brought down the dollar to between 35.685 rupees and 35.695 rupees. In the last 15 minutes of trading the RBI bought between $25 million and $50 million and pushed the dollar up between 35.7075 rupees and 35.7125 rupees by the end of trading. Foreign exchange dealers said fear of the Reserve Bank coming in to buy stopped the dollar from depreciating further.
MERCEDES TO IMPORT AUTO KITS AT 25 PERCENT

The Directorate General of Foreign Trade has given Mercedes Benz India a one-time advance licence to import completely knocked down kits at 25 percent value addition. The mandatory value addition level under the advance licence scheme is 33 percent. The licence and the special concession will be valid for a year. The company has agreed to comply with the 33 percent value addition obligation by next year. This is the first time an advance licence is awarded to a company that already has signed a memorandum of understanding to import such kits.
Financial Express
RESERVE BANK SETS EXPOSURE LIMIT TO TERM BORROWING

The Reserve Bank has set the term borrowing limit for a single borrower at 25 percent of the capital (equity plus free reserves) of the borrower. The limit set for group borrowers is 50 percent of the capital. The term-lending institutions were directed to reduce the existing credits which exceed the set limits by June 1998. The Reserve Bank also asked the institutions to bring such credits to the notice of the respective company's board of directors. This is the first time the RBI prescribed credit exposure limits for term lending institutions.
1:2 BONUS ISSUE OF EQUITY SHARES BY TATA SONS

Tata Sons Ltd, which is the holding company of the Tata group, will offer a 1:2 bonus issue of equity shares. The private company will issue up to 8,981,050 ordinary shares having a face value of 1,000 rupees each by capitalising up to 89.8 million rupees from the share premium account. The company is also stepping up dividend for the year ended March 1997 to 1,500 rupees a share from 1,000 rupees a share paid a year earlier.
Business Standard
RELIANCE TO LAUNCH 10 YEAR EUROBONDS

Petrochemical giant Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) will raise $100 million through a 10-year sterling denominated Eurobond issue. It will be priced above the UK treasury rate. The roadshows for the issue begin on Wednesday. The RIL has already raised about $900 million in overseas debt transactions. The present issue will be lead-managed by Merril Lynch, HSBC and UBS. The money will be used for its expansion plans at Hazira and Jamnagar in the state of Gujarat. The RIL last year completed a 90 billion rupee project in Hazira. It is building a large petrochemical complex at Jamnagar.
UNIT TRUST LAUNCHES SECTOR SPECIFIC OFFSHORE FUND

The Unit Trust of India (UTI) has launched a $50 million offshore fund dedicated to technology stocks. It is lead managed by Peregrine. The Trust has decided tentatively to invest 70 percent of the corpus in infotech stocks. The remaining 30 percent will be invested in the telecommunications sector. The fund will be launched in two tranches. A team of UTI fund managers are now in London. Reports from London say the response to the fund was favourable.
The Observer
TELECOM SERVICE PROVIDER INVITES NEW PROPOSALS

India's international telecom service provider Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) is inviting new proposals from AT&T, Unisource, BT-MCI and Sprint International to set up a new hub in India. The VSNL, which was planning to set up a joint venture with the British Telecom, is believed to have taken the new decision under pressure from the Communications Ministry. The ministry was insisting on transparency in the selection of partners for the joint venture. However, the British Telecom-VSNL joint venture proposal is awaiting clearance from the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
Business Line
EXPORTERS TO CHALLENGE EC MOVE ON ANIT-DUMPING DUTY

Cotton textiles exporters have decided to challenge the European Commission's move to impose anti-dumping duty on unbleached cotton fabrics from India. A team representing the exporters have rushed to the European Commission's headquarters in Brussels. The European Commission issued a notice on July 11 initiating anti-dumping proceedings on exports of unbleached cotton fabrics from India. A textile industry official expressed disappointment over the European Union's attempt to create trade barriers.
